nodes.name: kappa and rational approximation
nodes.statement: We set $\kappa \coloneqq 10^{-10}$ that  will be used throughout the remaining text, and we will write $\widetilde{x}\in \mathbb{Q}^{m\times n}$ for a rational approximation of $x\in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n}$ meaning that $\|x-\widetilde{x}\|\leq \kappa$.

nodes.name: kappa-rational approximation of a polyhedron
nodes.statement: Moreover, $\widetilde{\mathbf{P}} \subseteq \mathbb{Q}^3$ is a $\kappa$-rational approximation of $\mathbf{P} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ if each $\widetilde{P}_i \in \widetilde{\mathbf{P}}$ is a $\kappa$-rational approximation of the corresponding ${P}_i \in {\mathbf{P}}$.

nodes.name: Rational sine and cosine
nodes.statement:
We define the two functions $\sin_{\mathbb{Q}}, \cos_{\mathbb{Q}}: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ by:
    \begin{align*}
    \sin_{\mathbb{Q}}(x) & \coloneqq x-\frac{x^3}{3}+\frac{x^5}{5!}\mp \dots +\frac{x^{25}}{25!},\\
    \cos_{\mathbb{Q}}(x) & \coloneqq 1-\frac{x^2}{2}+\frac{x^4}{4!}\mp\dots +\frac{x^{24}}{24!}.
    \end{align*}
    Further, by replacing $\sin,\cos$ with $\sin_{\mathbb{Q}},\cos_{\mathbb{Q}}$ we define the functions 
\[
    R_{\mathbb{Q}}(\alpha), R'_{\mathbb{Q}}(\alpha), X_{\mathbb{Q}}(\theta, \varphi), M_{\mathbb{Q}}(\theta, \varphi), M_{\mathbb{Q}}^{\theta}(\theta,\varphi),M_{\mathbb{Q}}^{\varphi}(\theta,\varphi).
\]
nodes.statement_short: Taylor polynomials of degree 25/24 replacing $\sin,\cos$, and the resulting rational matrices $R_\mathbb{Q}, X_\mathbb{Q}, M_\mathbb{Q}$.

nodes.name: Accuracy of rational sine and cosine
nodes.statement:
For every $x\in [-4,4]$ it holds that
    \[
    |\sin_{\mathbb{Q}}(x)-\sin(x)| \leq \frac{\kappa}{7} \quad \text{and} \quad |\cos_{\mathbb{Q}}(x)-\cos(x)|\leq \frac{\kappa}{7}.
    \]
nodes.label: lem:kappa/7

nodes.name: Proof of rational sine/cosine accuracy
nodes.statement:
It is well known and not difficult to prove that for any $x \in \mathbb{R}$ one has
    \[
        |\sin_{\mathbb{Q}}(x)-\sin(x)|\leq \frac{|x|^{27}}{27!} \quad \text{as well as} \quad
    |\cos_{\mathbb{Q}}(x)-\cos(x)|\leq \frac{|x|^{26}}{26!}.
    \]
    As 
    ${4^{26}/26!}\approx 1.1\cdot 10^{-11}$ and ${4^{27}/27!}\approx 1.7\cdot 10^{-12}$ and $\kappa/7\approx 1.4\cdot 10^{-11}$ the claim is proven.
nodes.statement_short: Taylor remainder bounds evaluated at $|x|\le4$.

nodes.name: Entrywise bound on operator norm
nodes.statement: Let $A = (a_{i,j})_{1 \leq i \leq m,\ 1 \leq j \leq n} \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n}$ and $\delta >0$. Assume that $|a_{i,j}| \leq \delta$. Then it holds that $\|A\| \leq \delta \sqrt{mn}.$
assumptions: Let $A = (a_{i,j})_{1 \leq i \leq m,\ 1 \leq j \leq n} \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n}$ and $\delta >0$
nodes.label: lem:A<deltamn

nodes.name: Proof of entrywise norm bound
nodes.statement_short: Cauchy-Schwarz on each row.

nodes.name: Rational matrices approximate trigonometric matrices
nodes.statement:
Let $A(x,y)$ be an $m\times n$ matrix with $1 \leq m,n\leq 3$ such that every entry is of the form $a_1(x)\cdot a_2(y)$ where 
    $a_i(z)\in \{0,1,-1,\pm\sin(z),\pm\cos(z)\}.$
    Define $A_{\mathbb{Q}}(x,y)$ by replacing $\sin$ with $\sin_{\mathbb{Q}}$ and $\cos$ with $\cos_{\mathbb{Q}}$. Then for every $x,y\in[-4,4]$ it holds that
    $\|A(x,y)-A_\mathbb{Q}(x,y)\|\leq\kappa$.
assumptions:
Let $A(x,y)$ be an $m\times n$ matrix with $1 \leq m,n\leq 3$ such that every entry is of the form $a_1(x)\cdot a_2(y)$ where 
    $a_i(z)\in \{0,1,-1,\pm\sin(z),\pm\cos(z)\}.$
nodes.label: lem:dist<kappa

nodes.name: Proof of rational matrix approximation
nodes.statement:
For fixed $x,y$ every entry of $A(x,y)-A_{\mathbb{Q}}(x,y)$ is of the form
    $a b - \widetilde{a}\widetilde{b}$ for some $a,b\in[-1,1]$ and $|a-\widetilde{a}|,|b-\widetilde{b}|\leq \kappa/7$ by \cref{lem:kappa/7}. This implies that
    \begin{align*}
      |ab-\widetilde{a}\widetilde{b}|&\leq |a b-a\widetilde{b}|+|a \widetilde{b}-\widetilde{a}\widetilde{b}|
      =|a|\cdot |b-\widetilde{b}|+|\widetilde{b}|\cdot |a-\widetilde{a}| \leq 1\cdot \kappa/7+(1+\kappa/7) \cdot \kappa/7 <\kappa/3.
    \end{align*}
    So we can apply \cref{lem:A<deltamn} and obtain that $\|A(x,y)-A_{\mathbb{Q}}(x,y)\|<\kappa/3\cdot \sqrt{3\cdot 3}=\kappa$.
nodes.statement_short: Each entry differs by less than $\kappa/3$; then apply the entrywise norm bound.

nodes.name: kappa-accuracy of rational R, X, M and derivatives
nodes.statement:
Let $\alpha,\theta,\varphi\in [-4,4]$. Then it holds that
    \begin{align*}
        \|R(\alpha)-R_{\mathbb{Q}}(\alpha)\|, \|R'(\alpha)-R_{\mathbb{Q}}'(\alpha)\|,\|X(\theta,\varphi)-X_{\mathbb{Q}}(\theta, \varphi)\|, \|M(\theta, \varphi)-M_{\mathbb{Q}}(\theta, \varphi)\|, \\
        \|M^\theta(\theta,\varphi)-M_{\mathbb{Q}}^\theta(\theta,\varphi)\|,
        \|M^\varphi(\theta,\varphi) - M_{\mathbb{Q}}^\varphi(\theta,\varphi)\|\leq \kappa.
    \end{align*}
    Moreover,
    \[
        \|R_{\mathbb{Q}}(\alpha)\|, \|R'_{\mathbb{Q}}(\alpha)\|, \|X_{\mathbb{Q}}(\theta, \varphi)\|, \|M_{\mathbb{Q}}(\theta, \varphi)\|, \|M_{\mathbb{Q}}^{\theta}(\theta,\varphi)\|, \|M_{\mathbb{Q}}^{\varphi}(\theta,\varphi)\| \leq 1+\kappa.
    \]
nodes.label: corr:kappa1kappa

nodes.name: Proof of kappa-accuracy corollary
nodes.statement: The first statement is a direct application of \cref{lem:dist<kappa} and the second statement follows immediately after using \cref{lem:RaRalpha} and the triangle inequality.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the rational-matrix approximation lemma, then the unit-norm lemma and triangle inequality.

nodes.name: Product approximation bound
nodes.statement:
For $1 \leq i \leq n$ let $(A_i,B_i)$ be pairs of real matrices, such that for each $i$ the dimensions of $A_i$ and $B_i$ are equal. Assume moreover that the products $A_1\cdots A_n$ and $B_1 \cdots B_n$ are well defined. Finally, assume that $\|A_i-B_i\|\leq \kappa$ and let $\delta_i\geq \max(\|A_i\|,\|B_i\|,1)$. Then it holds that
    $\|A_1\cdots A_n-B_1\cdots B_n\|\leq n\kappa\cdot \delta_1\cdots \delta_n$.
nodes.statement_short: $\|A_1\cdots A_n-B_1\cdots B_n\|\le n\kappa\delta_1\cdots\delta_n$ when factors are $\kappa$-close.
assumptions: For $1 \leq i \leq n$ let $(A_i,B_i)$ be pairs of real matrices, such that for each $i$ the dimensions of $A_i$ and $B_i$ are equal
nodes.label: lem:A1AnB1Bn

nodes.name: Product bound applies to vectors and scalars
nodes.statement: Note, that this lemma can also be applied if some of the matrices are vectors or even scalars.

nodes.name: Proof of the product approximation bound
nodes.statement:
We prove the statement by induction on $n$. For $n=1$ the inequality $\|A_1-B_1\|\leq \kappa \delta_1$ is true since $\|A_1-B_1\|\leq \kappa$ and $\delta_1\geq 1$.

    Now let $\alpha_n \coloneqq \|A_1\cdots A_n-B_1\cdots B_n\|$. We find, using the triangle inequality, submultiplicativity of the norm and $\|A_i\|,\|B_i\| \leq \delta_i$ that
    \[
        \alpha_{n} \leq \| A_1 \cdots A_{n-1} \| \cdot \| A_{n} - B_{n} \| + \alpha_{n-1} \cdot \|B_{n}\| \leq \delta_1 \cdots \delta_{n-1} \cdot \kappa + \alpha_{n-1} \cdot \delta_{n}.
    \]
    By induction it holds that $\alpha_{n-1} \leq (n-1)\kappa \cdot \delta_1\cdots \delta_{n-1} $, thus we obtain that 
    \[
        \alpha_{n} \leq \delta_1 \cdots \delta_{n-1} \cdot \kappa + (n-1)\kappa \cdot \delta_1\cdots \delta_{n-1} \cdot \delta_{n} = \kappa \cdot \delta_1\cdots \delta_{n-1} \cdot (1 + (n-1) \delta_n) \leq n\kappa \cdot \delta_1\cdots \delta_n,
    \]
    using that $1 + (n-1) \delta_n \leq n\delta_n$.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on $n$ via a telescoping triangle-inequality step.

nodes.name: Rational Global Theorem
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathbf{P}$ be a pointsymmetric convex polyhedron with radius $\rho =1$ and $\widetilde{\mathbf{P}}$ a $\kappa$-rational approximation. Let $\widetilde{S} \in \widetilde{\mathbf{P}}$. Further let $\varepsilon>0$ and $\overline{\theta}_1,\overline{\varphi}_1,\overline{\theta}_2,\overline{\varphi}_2,\overline{\alpha} \in \mathbb{Q} \cap [-4,4]$.
    Let $w\in\mathbb{Q}^2$ be a unit vector. Denote $\overline{M_1} \coloneqq M_{\mathbb{Q}}(\overline{\theta}_1, \overline{\varphi}_1)$, $ \overline{M_2} \coloneqq M_{\mathbb{Q}}(\overline{\theta}_2, \overline{\varphi}_2)$ as well as $\overline{M_1}^{\theta} \coloneqq M_{\mathbb{Q}}^\theta(\overline{\theta}_1, \overline{\varphi}_1)$, $\overline{M_1}^{\varphi} \coloneqq M_{\mathbb{Q}}^\varphi(\overline{\theta}_1, \overline{\varphi}_1)$ and analogously for $\overline{M_2}^{\theta}, \overline{M_2}^{\varphi}$. Finally set
    \begin{align*}
        G^{\mathbb{Q}}& \coloneqq \langle R_{\mathbb{Q}}(\overline{\alpha}) \overline{M_1} \widetilde{S},w \rangle - \varepsilon\cdot\big(|\langle R_{\mathbb{Q}}'(\overline{\alpha})  \overline{M_1} \widetilde{S},w \rangle|+|\langle R_{\mathbb{Q}}(\overline{\alpha}) \overline{M_1}^\theta \widetilde{S},w \rangle|+|\langle R_{\mathbb{Q}}(\overline{\alpha}) \overline{M_1}^\varphi \widetilde{S},w \rangle|\big) \\
        & \hspace{11cm}- 9\varepsilon^2/2 - 4\kappa ( 1 + 3 \varepsilon),\\
        H^{\mathbb{Q}}_P & \coloneqq \langle \overline{M_2} P,w \rangle + \varepsilon\cdot\big(|\langle \overline{M_2}^\theta P,w \rangle|+|\langle  \overline{M_2}^\varphi P,w \rangle|\big) + 2\varepsilon^2 + 3\kappa( 1+2\varepsilon).
    \end{align*}
    If $G^{\mathbb{Q}}>\max_{P\in \widetilde{\mathbf{P}}} H^{\mathbb{Q}}_P$ then there does not exist a solution to Rupert's condition (\ref{eq:rupert_condition}) to $\mathbf{P}$ with 
    \[
    (\theta_1,\varphi_1,\theta_2,\varphi_2,\alpha) \in [\overline{\theta}_1\pm\varepsilon,\overline{\varphi}_1\pm\varepsilon,\overline{\theta}_2\pm\varepsilon,\overline{\varphi}_2\pm\varepsilon,\overline{\alpha}\pm\varepsilon].
    \]
nodes.statement_short: Rational version of the global theorem: with $\kappa$-corrections to $G$ and $H_P$, $G^\mathbb{Q}>\max H_P^\mathbb{Q}$ excludes the $\varepsilon$-cube.
assumptions: Let $\mathbf{P}$ be a pointsymmetric convex polyhedron with radius $\rho =1$ and $\widetilde{\mathbf{P}}$ a $\kappa$-rational approximation
conclusions:
then there does not exist a solution to Rupert's condition (\ref{eq:rupert_condition}) to $\mathbf{P}$ with 
    \[
    (\theta_1,\varphi_1,\theta_2,\varphi_2,\alpha) \in [\overline{\theta}_1\pm\varepsilon,\overline{\varphi}_1\pm\varepsilon,\overline{\theta}_2\pm\varepsilon,\overline{\varphi}_2\pm\varepsilon,\overline{\alpha}\pm\varepsilon].
    \]
nodes.label: thm:global_rational

nodes.name: Rational approximation bounds for scalar products
nodes.statement:
Let $\alpha, \theta, \varphi \in [-4,4]$, $P\in \mathbb{R}^3$ with $\|P\| \leq 1$ and let $\widetilde{P}$ be a $\kappa$-rational approximation of $P$. Set $M = M(\theta, \varphi)$ and $M_{\mathbb{Q}} = M_{\mathbb{Q}}(\theta, \varphi)$, $M^\theta = M^\theta(\theta, \varphi)$, $M^\theta_{\mathbb{Q}} = M^\theta_{\mathbb{Q}}(\theta, \varphi)$, $M^\varphi = M^\varphi(\theta, \varphi)$, $M^\varphi_{\mathbb{Q}} = M^\varphi_{\mathbb{Q}}(\theta, \varphi)$ as well as $R = R(\alpha)$, $R_{\mathbb{Q}} = R_{\mathbb{Q}}(\alpha)$, $R' = R'(\alpha)$, $R'_{\mathbb{Q}} = R'_{\mathbb{Q}}(\alpha)$. Finally let $w \in \mathbb{R}^2$ with $\|w\| = 1$. Then:
    \begin{align}
        | \langle M P, w\rangle - \langle M_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}, w\rangle | & \leq 3\kappa, \\
        | \langle M^\theta P, w\rangle - \langle M^\theta_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}, w\rangle | & \leq 3\kappa,\\
        | \langle M^\varphi P, w\rangle - \langle M^\varphi_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}, w\rangle | & \leq 3\kappa,\\
        | \langle R M P, w\rangle - \langle R_{\mathbb{Q}} M_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}, w\rangle | & \leq 4\kappa, \\
        | \langle R' M P, w\rangle - \langle R'_{\mathbb{Q}} M_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}, w\rangle | & \leq 4\kappa,\\
        | \langle R M^\theta P, w\rangle - \langle R_{\mathbb{Q}} M^\theta_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}, w\rangle | & \leq 4\kappa,\\
        | \langle R M^\varphi P, w\rangle - \langle R_{\mathbb{Q}} M^\varphi_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}, w\rangle | & \leq 4\kappa.
    \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Replacing $M, M^\theta, M^\varphi, R, R'$ and $P$ by rational approximations changes the scalar products with $w$ by at most $3\kappa$ or $4\kappa$.
conclusions:
\begin{align}
        | \langle M P, w\rangle - \langle M_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}, w\rangle | & \leq 3\kappa, \label{eq:boundskappa1} \\
        | \langle M^\theta P, w\rangle - \langle M^\theta_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}, w\rangle | & \leq 3\kappa,\\
        | \langle M^\varphi P, w\rangle - \langle M^\varphi_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}, w\rangle | & \leq 3\kappa,\\
        | \langle R M P, w\rangle - \langle R_{\mathbb{Q}} M_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}, w\rangle | & \leq 4\kappa,\label{eq:boundskappa4} \\
        | \langle R' M P, w\rangle - \langle R'_{\mathbb{Q}} M_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}, w\rangle | & \leq 4\kappa,\\
        | \langle R M^\theta P, w\rangle - \langle R_{\mathbb{Q}} M^\theta_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}, w\rangle | & \leq 4\kappa,\\
        | \langle R M^\varphi P, w\rangle - \langle R_{\mathbb{Q}} M^\varphi_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}, w\rangle | & \leq 4\kappa.
    \end{align}
nodes.label: lem:boundskappa

nodes.name: Rational scalar product bound (1)
nodes.statement: | \langle M P, w\rangle - \langle M_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}, w\rangle | & \leq 3\kappa,
nodes.label: eq:boundskappa1

nodes.name: Rational scalar product bound (2)
nodes.statement: | \langle M^\theta P, w\rangle - \langle M^\theta_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}, w\rangle | & \leq 3\kappa,

nodes.name: Rational scalar product bound (3)
nodes.statement: | \langle M^\varphi P, w\rangle - \langle M^\varphi_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}, w\rangle | & \leq 3\kappa,

nodes.name: Rational scalar product bound (4)
nodes.statement: | \langle R M P, w\rangle - \langle R_{\mathbb{Q}} M_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}, w\rangle | & \leq 4\kappa,
nodes.label: eq:boundskappa4

nodes.name: Rational scalar product bound (5)
nodes.statement: | \langle R' M P, w\rangle - \langle R'_{\mathbb{Q}} M_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}, w\rangle | & \leq 4\kappa,

nodes.name: Rational scalar product bound (6)
nodes.statement: | \langle R M^\theta P, w\rangle - \langle R_{\mathbb{Q}} M^\theta_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}, w\rangle | & \leq 4\kappa,

nodes.name: Rational scalar product bound (7)
nodes.statement: | \langle R M^\varphi P, w\rangle - \langle R_{\mathbb{Q}} M^\varphi_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}, w\rangle | & \leq 4\kappa.

nodes.name: Proof of the rational scalar product bounds
nodes.statement:
The proof is a direct application of \cref{lem:A1AnB1Bn}. We will only show (\ref{eq:boundskappa1}) and (\ref{eq:boundskappa4}) as the other inequalities are proven in a completely analogous way. 
    
    Using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality we obtain
    \[
        | \langle M P, w\rangle - \langle M_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}, w\rangle | = | \langle M P - M_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}, w\rangle | \leq \| MP - M_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P} \| \cdot \|w\|.
    \]
    Now observe that $\|w\|=1$ and $\| MP - M_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P} \| \leq 2 \kappa (1+\kappa)^2$ by \cref{lem:A1AnB1Bn} since $\|M_{\mathbb{Q}}\|, \|\widetilde{P}\| \leq 1 + \kappa$ by \cref{corr:kappa1kappa}. Then (\ref{eq:boundskappa1}) follows because $(1+\kappa)^2 < 3/2$.

    For (\ref{eq:boundskappa4}) it follows in the same way that 
    \[
        | \langle R M P, w\rangle - \langle R_{\mathbb{Q}} M_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}, w\rangle | \leq \|R M P - R_{\mathbb{Q}} M_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}\| \cdot \|w\|.
    \]
    Then \cref{lem:A1AnB1Bn} implies that $\|R M P - R_{\mathbb{Q}} M_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}\| \leq 3 \kappa (1 + \kappa)^3$ and the statement follows because $(1 + \kappa)^3 < 4/3$.
nodes.statement_short: Cauchy-Schwarz and the product approximation bound with $(1+\kappa)^k$ estimates.

nodes.name: Proof of the Rational Global Theorem
nodes.statement:
Let $G, H_{P}$ be the quantities in \cref{thm:global}. Then observe that 
    \[
        G \geq G^{\mathbb{Q}} \quad \text{ and } \quad H^{\mathbb{Q}}_P \geq H_P
    \]
    by \cref{lem:boundskappa}. It follows that, under the assumption of the theorem,  $G \geq G^{\mathbb{Q}} > \max_{P} H^{\mathbb{Q}}_P \geq  \max_{P} H_P$, thus we can apply \cref{thm:global} and conclude.
nodes.statement_short: $G\ge G^\mathbb{Q}$ and $H_P^\mathbb{Q}\ge H_P$ by the rational bounds, then apply the Global Theorem.

nodes.name: epsilon-kappa-spanning points
nodes.statement_short: Rational version of $\varepsilon$-spanning with an extra $6\kappa$ margin.
nodes.label: def:ekspanning

nodes.name: epsilon-kappa-spanning implies epsilon-spanning
nodes.statement: Let $P_1, P_2, P_3 \in \mathbb{R}^3$ with $\|P_i\| \leq 1$ and $\widetilde{P}_1, \widetilde{P}_2, \widetilde{P}_3 \in \mathbb{Q}^3$ be their $\kappa$-rational approximations. Assume that $\widetilde{P}_1, \widetilde{P}_2, \widetilde{P}_3$ are $\varepsilon$-$\kappa$-spanning for some $\theta, \varphi \in \mathbb{Q} \cap [-4,4]$, then $P_1, P_2, P_3$ are $\varepsilon$-spanning for $\theta, \varphi$.
assumptions: Let $P_1, P_2, P_3 \in \mathbb{R}^3$ with $\|P_i\| \leq 1$ and $\widetilde{P}_1, \widetilde{P}_2, \widetilde{P}_3 \in \mathbb{Q}^3$ be their $\kappa$-rational approximations
nodes.label: lem:ekspanningespanning

nodes.name: Proof that epsilon-kappa-spanning implies epsilon-spanning
nodes.statement:
Set $M \coloneqq M(\theta, \varphi)$ and $M_{\mathbb{Q}} \coloneqq M_{\mathbb{Q}}(\theta, \varphi)$. It suffices to show that  
    \begin{align} | \langle R(\pi/2) M P_1,M P_{2}\rangle - \langle R(\pi/2) M_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}_1,M_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}_{2}\rangle| \leq 6 \kappa,
    \end{align}
    since then 
    \[
        \langle R(\pi/2) M P_1,M P_{2}\rangle \geq \langle R(\pi/2) M_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}_1,M_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}_{2}\rangle - 6\kappa > 2 \varepsilon(\sqrt{2} + \varepsilon),
    \]
    analogously for the other two inequalities, and then \cref{lem:eps-spanning} concludes the proof.

    To see that inequality (\ref{eq:Rpi/2kappa}) holds true, note that the left-hand side can be written as 
    \[
        | P_2^t M^t R(\pi/2) M P_1 - \widetilde{P}^t_{2} M^t_{\mathbb{Q}} R(\pi/2) M_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}_1|, 
    \]
    which is bounded by $5 \kappa (1 + \kappa)^4 \leq 6\kappa$ with \cref{lem:A1AnB1Bn}.
nodes.statement_short: The rational and real cross-product terms differ by at most $6\kappa$ by the product approximation bound.

nodes.name: Rational spanning-term bound
nodes.statement: | \langle R(\pi/2) M P_1,M P_{2}\rangle - \langle R(\pi/2) M_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}_1,M_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}_{2}\rangle| \leq 6 \kappa,
nodes.label: eq:Rpi/2kappa

nodes.name: Upper and lower rational square roots
nodes.statement: We call a function $x \mapsto \sqrt[+]{x} : \mathbb{Q}_{\geq 0} \to \mathbb{Q}$ \emph{upper-$\mathbb{Q}$-square-root} if $\sqrt[+]{x} \geq \sqrt{x}$ for all $x \in \mathbb{Q}_{\geq0}$. Similarly $\sqrt[-]{x} : \mathbb{Q}_{\geq 0} \to \mathbb{Q}$ is called \emph{lower-$\mathbb{Q}$-square-root} if $\sqrt[-]{x} \leq \sqrt{x}$ for all $x \in \mathbb{Q}_{\geq 0}$.
nodes.label: def:sqrtplusminus

nodes.name: Rational Local Theorem
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathbf{P}$ be a polyhedron with radius $\rho=1$ and $\widetilde{P}_i$ be a $\kappa$-rational approximation of $P_i \in \mathbf{P}$. Set $\widetilde{\mathbf{P}} = \{\widetilde{P}_i \text{ for } P_i \in \mathbf{P} \}$. Let $P_1, P_2, P_3, Q_1, Q_2, Q_3 \in \mathbf{P}$ be not necessarily distinct and assume that $P_1, P_2, P_3$ and $Q_1, Q_2, Q_3$ are congruent. 
    Let $\varepsilon>0$ and $\overline{\theta}_1,\overline{\varphi}_1,\overline{\theta}_2,\overline{\varphi}_2,\overline{\alpha} \in \mathbb{Q} \cap [-4,4]$. 
    Set $\overline{X_1} \coloneqq X_{\mathbb{Q}}(\overline{\theta}_1,\overline{\varphi}_1), \overline{X_2} \coloneqq X_{\mathbb{Q}}(\overline{\theta}_2,\overline{\varphi}_2)$ as well as $\overline{M_1} \coloneqq M_{\mathbb{Q}}(\overline{\theta}_1,\overline{\varphi}_1), \overline{M_2} \coloneqq M_{\mathbb{Q}}(\overline{\theta}_2,\overline{\varphi}_2)$.
    Assume that there exist $\sigma_P, \sigma_Q \in \{0,1\}$ such that 
    \[
        (-1)^{\sigma_P} \langle \overline{X_1},\widetilde{P}_i\rangle>\sqrt{2}\varepsilon + 3\kappa \quad \text{and} \quad
        (-1)^{\sigma_Q} \langle \overline{X_2} , \widetilde{Q}_i\rangle>\sqrt{2}\varepsilon + 3\kappa, \tag{A$^{\mathbb{Q}}_\varepsilon$}
    \]
    for all $i=1,2,3$.
    Moreover, assume that $\widetilde{P}_1,\widetilde{P}_2,\widetilde{P}_3$ are $\varepsilon$-$\kappa$-spanning for $(\overline{\theta}_1,\overline{\varphi}_1)$ and that $\widetilde{Q}_1,\widetilde{Q}_2,\widetilde{Q}_3$ are $\varepsilon$-$\kappa$-spanning for $(\overline{\theta}_2,\overline{\varphi}_2)$. Let $\sqrt[+]{x}$ and $\sqrt[-]{x}$ be upper- and lower-$\mathbb{Q}$-square-root functions, then set $\|Z\|_{+} \coloneqq \sqrt[+]{\|Z\|^2}$ and $\|Z\|_{-} \coloneqq \sqrt[-]{\|Z\|^2}$ for $Z \in \mathbb{Q}^n$.
    Finally, assume that for all $i = 1,2,3$ and any $\widetilde{Q}_j \in \widetilde{\mathbf{P}} \setminus \widetilde{Q}_i$ it holds that 
    \[
        \frac{\langle \overline{M_2} \widetilde{Q}_i,\overline{M_2} (\widetilde{Q}_i-\widetilde{Q}_j)\rangle - 10\kappa - 2 \varepsilon ( \|\widetilde{Q}_i-\widetilde{Q}_j\|_{+} + 2 \kappa ) \cdot  (\sqrt{2}+\varepsilon)}{ \big(\|\overline{M_2} \widetilde{Q}_i\|_{+}+\sqrt{2} \varepsilon + 3\kappa \big) \cdot \big(\|\overline{M_2}(\widetilde{Q}_i-\widetilde{Q}_j)\|_{+}+2 \sqrt{2} \varepsilon + 6\kappa\big)} > \frac{\sqrt{5} \varepsilon + \delta}{r}, \tag{B$^{\mathbb{Q}}_\varepsilon$}
    \]
    for some $r >0$ such that $\min_{i=1,2,3}\| \overline{M_2} \widetilde{Q}_i \|_{-} > r + \sqrt{2} \varepsilon + 3\kappa$ and for some $\delta \in \mathbb{R}$ with 
    \[
        \delta = \max_{i=1,2,3}\left\|R_{\mathbb{Q}}(\overline{\alpha}) \overline{M_1} \widetilde{P}_i-\overline{M_2} \widetilde{Q}_i\right\|_{+}/2 + 3\kappa.
    \]
    Then there exists no solution to Rupert's problem $R(\alpha) M(\theta_1,\varphi_1)\mathbf{P} \subset  M(\theta_2,\varphi_2)\mathbf{P}^\circ$ with 
    \[
        (\theta_1, \varphi_1, \theta_2, \varphi_2, \alpha) \in [\overline{\theta}_1\pm\varepsilon,\overline{\varphi}_1\pm\varepsilon,\overline{\theta}_2\pm\varepsilon,\overline{\varphi}_2\pm\varepsilon,\overline{\alpha}\pm\varepsilon] \subseteq \mathbb{R}^5.
    \]
nodes.statement_short: Rational version of the local theorem with $\kappa$-corrected inequalities and rational square roots.
assumptions: Let $\mathbf{P}$ be a polyhedron with radius $\rho=1$
assume that $P_1, P_2, P_3$ and $Q_1, Q_2, Q_3$ are congruent

Assume that there exist $\sigma_P, \sigma_Q \in \{0,1\}$ such that 
    \[
        (-1)^{\sigma_P} \langle \overline{X_1},\widetilde{P}_i\rangle>\sqrt{2}\varepsilon + 3\kappa \quad \text{and} \quad
        (-1)^{\sigma_Q} \langle \overline{X_2} , \widetilde{Q}_i\rangle>\sqrt{2}\varepsilon + 3\kappa, \tag{A$^{\mathbb{Q}}_\varepsilon$}
    \]
    for all $i=1,2,3$

assume that $\widetilde{P}_1,\widetilde{P}_2,\widetilde{P}_3$ are $\varepsilon$-$\kappa$-spanning for $(\overline{\theta}_1,\overline{\varphi}_1)$ and that $\widetilde{Q}_1,\widetilde{Q}_2,\widetilde{Q}_3$ are $\varepsilon$-$\kappa$-spanning for $(\overline{\theta}_2,\overline{\varphi}_2)$

Finally, assume that for all $i = 1,2,3$ and any $\widetilde{Q}_j \in \widetilde{\mathbf{P}} \setminus \widetilde{Q}_i$ it holds that 
    \[
        \frac{\langle \overline{M_2} \widetilde{Q}_i,\overline{M_2} (\widetilde{Q}_i-\widetilde{Q}_j)\rangle - 10\kappa - 2 \varepsilon ( \|\widetilde{Q}_i-\widetilde{Q}_j\|_{+} + 2 \kappa ) \cdot  (\sqrt{2}+\varepsilon)}{ \big(\|\overline{M_2} \widetilde{Q}_i\|_{+}+\sqrt{2} \varepsilon + 3\kappa \big) \cdot \big(\|\overline{M_2}(\widetilde{Q}_i-\widetilde{Q}_j)\|_{+}+2 \sqrt{2} \varepsilon + 6\kappa\big)} > \frac{\sqrt{5} \varepsilon + \delta}{r}, \tag{B$^{\mathbb{Q}}_\varepsilon$}
    \]
    for some $r >0$ such that $\min_{i=1,2,3}\| \overline{M_2} \widetilde{Q}_i \|_{-} > r + \sqrt{2} \varepsilon + 3\kappa$ and for some $\delta \in \mathbb{R}$ with 
    \[
        \delta = \max_{i=1,2,3}\left\|R_{\mathbb{Q}}(\overline{\alpha}) \overline{M_1} \widetilde{P}_i-\overline{M_2} \widetilde{Q}_i\right\|_{+}/2 + 3\kappa.
    \]
conclusions:
Then there exists no solution to Rupert's problem $R(\alpha) M(\theta_1,\varphi_1)\mathbf{P} \subset  M(\theta_2,\varphi_2)\mathbf{P}^\circ$ with 
    \[
        (\theta_1, \varphi_1, \theta_2, \varphi_2, \alpha) \in [\overline{\theta}_1\pm\varepsilon,\overline{\varphi}_1\pm\varepsilon,\overline{\theta}_2\pm\varepsilon,\overline{\varphi}_2\pm\varepsilon,\overline{\alpha}\pm\varepsilon] \subseteq \mathbb{R}^5.
    \]
nodes.label: thm:local_rational

nodes.name: Rational bounds for the local theorem quantities
assumptions: Let $P,Q \in \mathbb{R}^3$ with $\|P\|,\|Q\|\leq 1$ and $\widetilde{P},\widetilde{Q}$ some respective $\kappa$-rational approximations
nodes.label: lem:boundskappa3

nodes.name: Rational local bound (1)
nodes.statement: |\langle X, P \rangle - \langle X_{\mathbb{Q}}, \widetilde{P} \rangle| & \leq 3 \kappa,
nodes.label: eq:boundskappa3.1

nodes.name: Rational local bound (2)
nodes.statement: |\langle MP, MQ \rangle - \langle M_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}, M_{\mathbb{Q}}\widetilde{Q} \rangle| & \leq 5 \kappa,
nodes.label: eq:boundskappa3.3

nodes.name: Rational local bound (3)
nodes.statement: |\| M Q \| - \| M_{\mathbb{Q}}\widetilde{Q} \| | & \leq 3 \kappa.
nodes.label: eq:boundskappa3.2

nodes.name: Proof of the rational local bounds
nodes.statement:
Note that if $\|P\| \leq 1$ then $\|\widetilde{P}\| \leq 1 + \kappa$. Rewrite (\ref{eq:boundskappa3.1}) as $ | P^t X - \widetilde{P}^t X_{\mathbb{Q}} | $ and then observe that \cref{lem:A1AnB1Bn} yields the bound $2 \kappa (1 + \kappa)^2 \leq 3\kappa$.

    Inequality (\ref{eq:boundskappa3.3}) follows in a similar way by rewriting the left-hand side as $| Q^t M^t MP -  \widetilde{Q}^t M_{\mathbb{Q}}^t M_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P} |$, applying \cref{lem:A1AnB1Bn} and using that $4 \kappa (1+\kappa)^4 \leq 5\kappa$.

    Finally for (\ref{eq:boundskappa3.2}), observe that by the reverse triangle inequality it holds that $|\| M Q \| - \| M_{\mathbb{Q}}\widetilde{Q} \| |\leq \| MQ - M_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{Q} \| $ and the latter is bounded by $2 \kappa (1 + \kappa)^2 \leq  3\kappa$ using \cref{lem:A1AnB1Bn}.
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite each quantity as a matrix product and apply the product approximation bound.

nodes.name: Rational bound for delta
nodes.statement:
In the setting of  \cref{lem:boundskappa3} let additionally $\overline{\theta}, \overline{\varphi} \in \mathbb{R} \cap [-4,4]$ and set $\overline{M} = M(\overline{\theta}, \overline{\varphi})$, $\overline{M}_{\mathbb{Q}} = M_{\mathbb{Q}}(\overline{\theta}, \overline{\varphi})$. Then
    \[
    |\| R(\alpha) M P - \overline{M} Q\|- \| R_{\mathbb{Q}}(\alpha) M_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P} - \overline{M}_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{Q}\| | \leq 6 \kappa. \]
nodes.label: corr:deltakappa

nodes.name: Proof of the rational delta bound
nodes.statement:
Using $\big| \|a-b\| - \|c-d\|\big| \leq \|a-c\| + \|b-d\|$ we first bound the left-hand side by 
    \[
        \| R(\alpha) M P - R_{\mathbb{Q}}(\alpha) M_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P} \| + \| \overline{M} Q - \overline{M}_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{Q}\|,
    \]
    then apply (\ref{eq:boundskappa3.2}) and the same proof as of (\ref{eq:boundskappa4}) to obtain the desired bound $ 3\kappa + 3\kappa = 6 \kappa$.
nodes.statement_short: Split by the triangle inequality and bound each term by $3\kappa$.

nodes.name: Rational lower bound for the cosine quotient
nodes.statement:
In the setting of \cref{lem:boundskappa3}, let $\sqrt[+]{x}$ be an upper-$\mathbb{Q}$-square-root function and set $\|x\|_{+} \coloneqq \sqrt[+]{\|x\|^2}$. Set
    \[
        A =  \frac{\langle M P, M(P-Q)\rangle - 2 \varepsilon  \|P-Q\| \cdot  (\sqrt{2}+\varepsilon)}{ \big(\| M P\|+\sqrt{2} \varepsilon \big) \cdot \big(\|M(P-Q)\|+2 \sqrt{2} \varepsilon\big)} 
    \]
    as well as 
    \[
        A_{\mathbb{Q}} =         \frac{\langle M_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}, M_{\mathbb{Q}} (\widetilde{P}-\widetilde{Q})\rangle - 10\kappa - 2 \varepsilon ( \|\widetilde{P}-\widetilde{Q}\|_{+} + 2 \kappa ) \cdot  (\sqrt{2}+\varepsilon)}{ \big(\| M_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}\|_{+}+\sqrt{2} \varepsilon + 3\kappa \big) \cdot \big(\|M_{\mathbb{Q}}(\widetilde{P}-\widetilde{Q})\|_{+}+2 \sqrt{2} \varepsilon + 6\kappa\big)}.
    \]
    Assuming that $A_{\mathbb{Q}} > 0$, it then holds that $A \geq A_{\mathbb{Q}}$.
nodes.statement_short: The rational quotient $A_\mathbb{Q}$, when positive, is a lower bound for the real quotient $A$.
nodes.label: lem:boundskappa4

nodes.name: Proof of the rational cosine quotient bound
nodes.statement:
Note that $(\widetilde{P}-\widetilde{Q})/2$ is a $\kappa$-rational approximation of $(P-Q)/2$ and that $\|(P-Q)/2\| \leq 1$. Therefore, by \cref{lem:boundskappa3}'s inequality (\ref{eq:boundskappa3.3}) it holds that 
    \[
       \bigg| \Big \langle M P, M \frac{P-Q}{2} \Big \rangle - \Big \langle M_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}, M_{\mathbb{Q}} \frac{\widetilde{P}-\widetilde{Q}}{2} \Big \rangle \bigg | \leq  5\kappa,
    \]
    and consequently we obtain that 
    \[
        \langle M P, M (P-Q) \rangle \geq \langle M P, M (\widetilde{P}-\widetilde{Q}) \rangle - 10\kappa.
    \]
    Further, the triangle inequality implies that 
    \[
        \|P-Q\| \leq \|\widetilde{P}-\widetilde{Q}\| + 2 \kappa \leq \|\widetilde{P}-\widetilde{Q}\|_{+} + 2 \kappa.
    \]
    It follows that the numerator of $A_{\mathbb{Q}}$ is at most the numerator of $A$ and that both are positive. 

    Finally, (\ref{eq:boundskappa3.2}) implies that 
    \[
        \| M P\| \leq \| M_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}\| + 3\kappa \leq \|  M_{\mathbb{Q}} \widetilde{P}\|_{+} + 3\kappa, 
    \]
    and also that 
    \[
        \| M (P-Q)\| = 2\Big \| M \frac{P-Q}{2} \Big\| \leq 2 \Big \| M_{\mathbb{Q}} \frac{\widetilde{P} - \widetilde{Q}}{2} \Big\| + 6\kappa \leq \|  M_{\mathbb{Q}} (\widetilde{P} - \widetilde{Q})\|_{+} + 6\kappa.
    \]
    Therefore, the denominator of $A$ is at most the denominator of $A_{\mathbb{Q}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Show the numerator of $A_\mathbb{Q}$ is at most that of $A$ and the denominator at least, using the rational local bounds.

nodes.name: Proof of the Rational Local Theorem
nodes.statement:
We shall show that we may apply \cref{thm:local}. 
    
    The inequalities in (A$^{\mathbb{Q}}_\varepsilon$) imply (A$_\varepsilon$) thanks to (\ref{eq:boundskappa3.1}) in \cref{lem:boundskappa3}. Similarly, (B$^{\mathbb{Q}}_\varepsilon$) implies (B$_\varepsilon$) by \cref{lem:boundskappa4}. Note that the bound on $r$ uses (\ref{eq:boundskappa3.2}) and the bound for $\delta$ uses \cref{corr:deltakappa}. The assumption that $\widetilde{P}_1,\widetilde{P}_2,\widetilde{P}_3$ are $\varepsilon$-$\kappa$-spanning implies that $P_1,P_2,P_3$ are $\varepsilon$-spanning by \cref{lem:ekspanningespanning}, and analogously for $Q_1,Q_2,Q_3$.
nodes.statement_short: Each rational hypothesis implies the corresponding hypothesis of the Local Theorem, which then applies.

nodes.name: Computer-assisted proof that the Noperthedron is not Rupert
nodes.statement:
In \cref{cor:NOPbounds} of \cref{sec:noperthedron} we have proven that if $\mathbf{NOP}$ was Rupert then there would exists a solution to its Rupert's condition (\ref{eq:rupert_condition}) with  
\begin{align*}    
\theta_1,\theta_2&\in[0,2\pi/15] \subset [0,0.42], \\
\varphi_1&\in [0,\pi] \subset [0,3.15],\\
\varphi_2&\in [0,\pi/2] \subset [0,1.58],\\
\alpha &\in [-\pi/2,\pi/2] \subset [-1.58,1.58].
\end{align*}

Generally speaking, in order to prove that a solution for any solid $\mathbf{P}$ does not exist within any given five dimensional interval for $[\overline{\theta}_1, \overline{\varphi}_1, \overline{\theta}_2, \overline{\varphi}_2, \overline{\alpha}] \pm \varepsilon \subseteq \mathbb{R}^5$, we can establish 3 (recursive) options:
\begin{itemize}
    \item [(I)] Apply the (rational) global theorem (\cref{thm:global}),
    \item [(II)] Apply the (rational) local theorem (\cref{thm:local}),
    \item [(III)] Subdivide the interval into smaller intervals, and for each of them again apply one of (I)--(III).
\end{itemize}

To show that the Noperthedron is not Rupert, one can now think of creating a ``solution tree'' with each node corresponding to some interval and the root of the tree representing the initial interval from \cref{cor:NOPbounds}. 
If a node/interval can be proven to not contain a solution (using the global or the local theorems) then this node is a leaf. Otherwise, one might write the interval as a union of smaller intervals, each of which is then one of its children.

For $\mathbf{NOP}$ we have created such a tree algorithmically in the programming language \href{https://www.r-project.org/}{R} using floating point operations. 
On a good PC this took roughly 7 hours and used less than 4 GB of RAM. This tree has 585\,200 interior nodes and 18\,115\,245 leaf nodes, 17\,492\,530 of which can be solved using the global theorem and 622\,715 of which using the local theorem. It is stored in the form of a tabular database such that each of its rows corresponds to one node. Additionally, we store information about how the rational global/local theorems can be applied. 
The generation code and solution file can be found in \href{https://github.com/Jakob256/Rupert}{www.github.com/Jakob256/Rupert} with an excerpt of the latter displayed in \cref{tab:solution_tree} below. In \cref{sec:structure} we explain more details about the  structure of the solution tree.

Note that the floating point driven \href{https://www.r-project.org/}{R} code is not part of the proof of \cref{thm:main}: The algorithmic rigorous verification of the solution tree was programmed in \href{https://www.sagemath.org/}{SageMath}. This code checks that the rational versions of the global and local theorems can be applied to each leaf and that the union of them is the initial interval. This step is computationally more expensive and takes about 30 hours on the same PC. In \cref{sec:verification} we explain this code which is available on \href{https://github.com/Jakob256/Rupert}{www.github.com/Jakob256/Rupert}.


\subsection{Structure of the solution tree} As mentioned above, our tabular solution tree for the Noperthedron contains all necessary information needed for proving that this solid does not have Rupert's property. Each of its rows corresponds to a five-dimensional interval for a possible solution $(\theta_1, \varphi_1, \theta_2, \varphi_2, \alpha)$ with an indication which of the three options above (I), (II), (III) to apply. In the subdivision case (III) the data in the row points to the children of the node and in the cases (I) and (II) the row contains information on how to apply the global or local theorems to the interval. 
More precisely, the table has the following~columns:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{ID}: Is a unique consecutive number for each row.
    \item \textbf{nodeType}: A number 1, 2 or 3, corresponding to the options (I), (II) or (III) above. 
    \item \textbf{nrChildren}: In the subdivision case (nodeType=3), the number of children this node has.
    \item \textbf{IDfirstChild}: In the case nodeType=3, the ID of the first child node. The children are stored as consequentive rows, therefore nrChildren and IDfirstChild are enough to recover~them. 
    \item \textbf{split}: When nodeType=3, for convenience, we store a variable which records how the interval is going to be split. There are the following options:
    \begin{align*}
        \text{split} =1 & \iff \text{only the interval for } \overline{\theta}_1 \text{ is split},\\
        \text{split} =2 & \iff \text{only the interval for } \overline{\varphi}_1 \text{ is split},\\
        \text{split} =3 & \iff \text{only the interval for } \overline{\theta}_2 \text{ is split},\\
        \text{split} =4 & \iff \text{only the interval for } \overline{\varphi}_2 \text{ is split},\\
        \text{split} =5 & \iff \text{only the interval for } \overline{\alpha} \text{ is split},\\
        \text{split} =6 & \iff \text{all five intervals are split in half}.
    \end{align*}
    In other words, for $\mathrm{split} \in \{1,\dots,5\}$ the corresponding interval is divided in nrChildren equal parts, whereas if $\mathrm{split}=6$ then all intervals are halved resulting in $\mathrm{nrChildren}=2^5 = 32$. 
    \item \textbf{T1\_min}, \textbf{T1\_max}, \textbf{V1\_min}, \textbf{V1\_max}, \textbf{T2\_min}, \textbf{T2\_max}, \textbf{V2\_min}, \textbf{V2\_max}, \textbf{A\_min}, \textbf{A\_max} are the numerators of the boundaries for the interval of the node/row:
    \begin{align*}
        N \cdot \theta_1 & \in [T1_{\min}, T1_{\max} ], \\ 
        N \cdot\varphi_1 & \in [V1_{\min}, V1_{\max} ], \\
        N \cdot\theta_2 & \in [T2_{\min}, T2_{\max} ], \\ 
        N \cdot\varphi_2 & \in [V2_{\min}, V2_{\max} ], \\ 
        N \cdot\alpha & \in [A_{\min}, A_{\max} ],
    \end{align*}
    with $N$ set to 15\,360\,000.
    \item \textbf{S\_index}: The index of the vertex $S$ for applying the (rational) global theorem (\cref{thm:global_rational}), used if nodeType=1.
    \item \textbf{wx\_nominator}, \textbf{wy\_nominator}, \textbf{w\_denominator} are the numerators and common denominator of the components of the unit vector $w = (w_x, w_y) \in \mathbb{Q}^2$ in \cref{thm:global_rational} (present if nodeType=1).
    \item \textbf{P1\_index}, \textbf{P2\_index}, \textbf{P3\_index}, \textbf{Q1\_index}, \textbf{Q2\_index}, \textbf{Q3\_index}: The indices of the congruent triples $P_1,P_2,P_3,Q_1,Q_2,Q_3 \in \mathbf{NOP}$ from \cref{thm:local_rational}, used if nodeType=2.
    \item \textbf{r}, \textbf{sigma\_Q}: The numerator $r'$ of the rational number $r = r'/1000 \in \mathbb{Q}$ and $\sigma_Q \in \{0,1\}$ from \cref{thm:local_rational} (if nodeType=2).
\end{enumerate}

Note that all entries of the table are integers, therefore no rounding loss occurs when loading or storing it. 
When talking about \textit{indices of vertices} we refer to the ordering $\mathbf{NOP} = (P_0, \dots, P_{89})$ defined as
\begin{align} P_{k+15i+45 \ell}=(-1)^\ell R_z\left(\frac{2\pi k}{15}\right)C_{i+1}
\quad \text{ for } \quad i \in \{0,1,2\}, \; k \in \{0,\dots,14\}, \; \ell \in \{0,1\},
\end{align}
and $C_1, C_2, C_3 \in \mathbb{Q}^3$ given in \cref{sec:noperthedron}. Moreover, we always assume that $\sigma_{P} = 0$, so we only store~$\sigma_Q \in \{0,1\}$. 

A small excerpt of the solution tree is displayed in \cref{tab:solution_tree}. We note that stored as a \textit{csv} file it takes roughly 2.5 GB of storage space. A zipped version of it can be downloaded from \href{https://github.com/Jakob256/Rupert}{www.github.com/Jakob256/Rupert}.

\subsection{Verification} In order to verify that the solution tree indeed proves \cref{thm:main} we must check the following assertions:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item[(A)] The union of all leaf intervals (rows with nodeType=1 or 2) contains the interval in \cref{cor:NOPbounds},
    \item[(B)] For each row with nodeType=1 one can apply \cref{thm:global_rational} and for each row with nodeType=2 one can apply \cref{thm:local_rational}.
\end{enumerate}

In order to check (A) we first verify that for each node the union of all its children contains its interval. Further we check that all nodes are either leafs (nodeType=1 or 2) or interval nodes (nodeType=3), and that the root contains the interval in \cref{cor:NOPbounds}. With the fact that the ID of any child is always strictly larger than the ID of the parent, this proves (A).

The verification of (B) splits into two cases: nodeType=1 or nodeType=2. They are explained in \cref{sec:veriglob} and \cref{sec:veriloc}. For each of them $\widetilde{\mathbf{NOP}}$ is defined as the following truncation of all vertices of $\mathbf{NOP}$ to 16 decimal places and is therefore a $\kappa$-rational approximation:
\[
    \widetilde{\mathbf{NOP}} \coloneqq \lfloor10^{16} \cdot \mathbf{NOP} \rfloor /10^{16}.
\]
The indices correspond to points via the ordering in (\ref{eq:ordering}). Both cases start with the following two operations:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Set $N=15\,360\,000$ and compute 
    \begin{align*}
    \overline{\theta}_1 & = (T1_{\min} + T1_{\max} )/(2N), \\ 
    \overline{\varphi}_1 & = (V1_{\min} + V1_{\max} )/(2N), \\
    \overline{\theta}_2 & = (T2_{\min} + T2_{\max} )/(2N), \\ 
    \overline{\varphi}_2 & = (V2_{\min} + V2_{\max} )/(2N), \\ 
    \overline{\alpha} & = (A_{\min} + A_{\max} )/(2N).
\end{align*}
Check that $\overline{\theta}_i, \overline{\varphi}_i, \overline{\alpha} \in [-4,4]$.
\item Set $\varepsilon = \max(T1_{\max} - T1_{\min}, V1_{\max} - V1_{\min},T2_{\max} - T2_{\min}, V1_{\max} - V1_{\min}, A_{\max} - A_{\min})/(2N)$.
\end{enumerate}

\subsubsection{Verification of the global theorem} The verification of the rational global theorem (\cref{thm:global_rational}) is relatively straightforward. Namely, for every row in the solution tree which has noteType=1 we must perform the following operations (additionally to 1. and 2. above):
\begin{enumerate}
    \setcounter{enumi}{2}
    \item Set $w = ($wx\_numerator/w\_denominator, wy\_numerator/w\_denominator$) \in \mathbb{Q}^2$ and check that $\|w\|^2 = w_1^2 + w_2^2=1$.
    \item Set $\widetilde{S}$ to be the rationally approximated point corresponding to the index given in column~S\_index.
    \item Compute $\overline{M_1}$, $\overline{M_2}$, $\overline{M_1}^\theta$, $\overline{M_1}^\varphi$, $\overline{M_2}^\theta$, $\overline{M_2}^\varphi \in \mathbb{Q}^{2 \times 3}$ and $R_{\mathbb{Q}}(\overline{\alpha}), R'_{\mathbb{Q}}(\overline{\alpha}) \in \mathbb{Q}^{2 \times 2}$ as in \cref{thm:global_rational}.
    \item Compute $G^{\mathbb{Q}} \in \mathbb{Q}$ and $H_{P}^{\mathbb{Q}} \in \mathbb{Q}$ for all $P \in \widetilde{\mathbf{NOP}}$ as in \cref{thm:global_rational}.
    \item Verify that $G^{\mathbb{Q}} > \max H_{P}^{\mathbb{Q}}$.
\end{enumerate}

Note that all steps only use rational numbers, thus in the computer algebra system \href{https://www.sagemath.org/}{SageMath} no rounding loss or precision errors can occur.

\subsubsection{Verification of the local theorem} For the verification of the rational local \cref{thm:local_rational} for all rows of the solution tree with nodeType=2 we have to perform more work.

First, recall that in \cref{def:sqrtplusminus} and \cref{thm:local_rational} we define/use the upper- and lower-square root functions $\sqrt[+]{x}, \sqrt[-]{x} \colon \mathbb{Q}_{\geq 0} \to \mathbb{Q}_{\geq 0}$ given via
    \[
        \sqrt[-]{x} \leq \sqrt{x} \leq \sqrt[+]{x}.
    \]
    We decided to implement the following functions since they allow a precise control on the size of the denominator/accuracy and at the same time can be relatively efficiently implemented: 
    
    First, set $\sqrt[-]{0}=\sqrt[+]{0}=0$. For any $x>0$, there exists a unique $a\in \mathbb{Z}$ such that 
    \[
        x \cdot 10^{2a}\in [10^{20},10^{22}),
    \]
    and then there exists a unique $b\in \mathbb{Z}^+$ such that 
    \[
        b^2\leq x\cdot 10^{2a} < (b+1)^2.
    \]
    Observe that $b/10^a \leq \sqrt{x}$, so we define 
    \begin{align} \sqrt[-]{x} \coloneqq \frac{b}{10^a} \quad \text{and} \quad \sqrt[+]{x} \coloneqq \frac{1}{\sqrt[-]{1/x}}.
    \end{align}
    We then also define 
    \[
        \|Z\|_{-} \coloneqq \sqrt[-]{\|Z\|^2} \quad \text{ and } \quad \|Z\|_{+} \coloneqq \sqrt[+]{\|Z\|^2}
    \]
    for any $Z \in \mathbb{Q}^{n}$, so that $\|Z\|_{-},\|Z\|_{+} \in \mathbb{Q}$ and $\|Z\|_{-} \leq \|Z\| \leq \|Z\|_{+}$. \\

    Similarly to the global theorem verification after the steps 1. and 2. above, we perform the following steps for each row with nodeType=2:

    \begin{enumerate}
    \setcounter{enumi}{2}
    \item Check that $P_1,P_2,P_3$ and $Q_1,Q_2,Q_3$ are congruent by applying \cref{lem:congruent} (verifying that $P^tP = Q^tQ$ and $\det(Q) \neq 0$).
    \item Compute $\overline{M_1}$, $\overline{M_2} \in \mathbb{Q}^{2 \times 3}$, $\overline{X_1}, \overline{X_2} \in \mathbb{Q}^{3}$ and $R_{\mathbb{Q}}(\overline{\alpha}) \in \mathbb{Q}^{2 \times 2}$ as in \cref{thm:global_rational}.
    \item Set $\sigma_Q =$ sigma\_Q and check that 
    \[
        \langle \overline{X_1}, \widetilde{P}_i\rangle>\sqrt{2}\varepsilon + 3 \kappa \quad \text{ and } \quad (-1)^{\sigma_Q} \langle \overline{X_2},\widetilde{P}_i\rangle>\sqrt{2}\varepsilon +3 \kappa.
    \]
    \item Check that $\widetilde{P}_1,\widetilde{P}_2,\widetilde{P}_3$ are $\varepsilon$-$\kappa$-spanning for $(\overline{\theta}_1, \overline{\varphi}_1)$ and that $\widetilde{Q}_1,\widetilde{Q}_2,\widetilde{Q}_3$ are $\varepsilon$-$\kappa$-spanning for $(\overline{\theta}_2, \overline{\varphi}_2)$ by verifying the inequalities in \cref{def:ekspanning}:
        \begin{align*}
                \langle R(\pi/2) \overline{M_1} \widetilde{P}_1, \overline{M_1} \widetilde{P}_{2}\rangle > 2 \varepsilon(\sqrt{2} + \varepsilon) + 6\kappa,\\
                \langle R(\pi/2) \overline{M_1} \widetilde{P}_2, \overline{M_1} \widetilde{P}_{3}\rangle > 2 \varepsilon(\sqrt{2} + \varepsilon) + 6\kappa,\\
                \langle R(\pi/2) \overline{M_1} \widetilde{P}_3, \overline{M_1} \widetilde{P}_{1}\rangle > 2 \varepsilon(\sqrt{2} + \varepsilon) + 6\kappa,
        \end{align*}
        and 
            \begin{align*}
                \langle R(\pi/2) \overline{M_2} \widetilde{Q}_1, \overline{M_2} \widetilde{Q}_{2}\rangle > 2 \varepsilon(\sqrt{2} + \varepsilon) + 6\kappa,\\
                \langle R(\pi/2) \overline{M_2} \widetilde{Q}_2, \overline{M_2} \widetilde{Q}_{3}\rangle > 2 \varepsilon(\sqrt{2} + \varepsilon) + 6\kappa,\\
                \langle R(\pi/2) \overline{M_2} \widetilde{Q}_3, \overline{M_2} \widetilde{Q}_{1}\rangle > 2 \varepsilon(\sqrt{2} + \varepsilon) + 6\kappa.
        \end{align*}
    \item Set $r = r'/1000 \in \mathbb{Q}$ with $r'$ taken from the r column and define
        \[
            \delta = \max_{i=1,2,3}\left\|R_{\mathbb{Q}}(\overline{\alpha}) \overline{M_1} \widetilde{P}_i-\overline{M_2} \widetilde{Q}_i\right\|_{+}/2 + 3\kappa \in \mathbb{Q}.
        \]
    \item Check that $\| \overline{M_2} \widetilde{Q}_i \|_{-} > r + \sqrt{2} \varepsilon + 3\kappa$ for $i=1,2,3$.
    \item Finally verify that 
    \[
        \frac{\langle \overline{M_2} \widetilde{Q}_i,\overline{M_2} (\widetilde{Q}_i-\widetilde{Q}_j)\rangle - 10\kappa - 2 \varepsilon ( \|\widetilde{Q}_i-\widetilde{Q}_j\|_{+} + 2 \kappa ) \cdot  (\sqrt{2}+\varepsilon)}{ \big(\|\overline{M_2} \widetilde{Q}_i\|_{+}+\sqrt{2} \varepsilon + 3\kappa \big) \cdot \big(\|\overline{M_2}(\widetilde{Q}_i-\widetilde{Q}_j)\|_{+}+2 \sqrt{2} \varepsilon + 6 \kappa\big)} > \frac{\sqrt{5} \varepsilon + \delta}{r},
    \]
    for all $i = 1,2,3$ and any $\widetilde{Q}_j \in \widetilde{\mathbf{NOP}} \setminus \widetilde{Q}_i$.
\end{enumerate}

Note that $\sqrt{2}$ in the steps 5., 6., 8. and 9. can be approximated by $142/100 = 1.42 > \sqrt{2}$ making the inequalities stricter and the expressions rational. Similarly, we approximate $\sqrt{5}$ in step 9. by $224/100 = 2.24 > \sqrt{5}$, so that also this condition becomes a statement on purely rational numbers. It follows that the only non-rational condition to check is step 3., namely that 
\(
P^tP = Q^tQ
\)
for $P = (P_1|P_2|P_3) \in \overline{\mathbb{Q}}^{3 \times 3}$, $Q = (Q_1|Q_2|Q_3)\in \overline{\mathbb{Q}}^{3 \times 3}$ and that $\det(Q) \neq 0$. Note that these expressions are, however, over algebraic numbers and \href{https://www.sagemath.org/}{SageMath} can prove them relatively~quickly. 

\bigskip

We implemented the verification of the solution tree integrity as well as the procedures of \cref{sec:veriglob} and \cref{sec:veriloc} in \href{https://www.sagemath.org/}{SageMath}. The total run time of this code is roughly 30h on a good PC which roughly consists of 1h for the solution tree integrity check, 16h of verification of rational global theorems and 10h of rational local theorems verification. 
This finally finishes the proof of \cref{thm:main}.
